description: Reformation remaps five way point voltages of an incoming signal to new values and interpolates everything in between, then drives, clips and attenuates the result

params.text: Amplifies the remapped signal before clipping, from 1 for no amplification to 10, with a default of 2; the Drive input adds to it and the total is clamped to that range
Attenuates the signal after drive and clipping, 0 to 1, multiplied by the Level input divided by 10V; the default of 0.5 cancels the default drive of 2
Sets the polarity expected at the signal input, green for unipolar 0-10V and red for bipolar -5V to 5V, which fixes the input voltage each way point stands for
Sets the polarity of the final output, green for unipolar and red for bipolar; unipolar output is offset by +5V, and it can go below 0V unless clipping is switched on
Sets the clipping applied after the drive: grey for none, yellow for hard clipping at 10V either way, orange for soft tanh clipping at 10V either way
Sets oversampling against the aliasing the remapping and clipping introduce: grey for off, light blue for x4, dark blue for x8
Sets the voltage that its way point of the input is remapped to; the bold line on the scale marks no change, and voltages between way points are interpolated
Attenuates or inverts one of the two CV inputs for that way point, -1 to +1, and the result is summed with the slider to give the effective mapping

inputs.text: A bipolar CV input for one way point, attenuated by its own attenuverter and summed with the slider; the sum is unconstrained, so the mapping can leave the normal ranges
Added to the Drive knob, the total clamped between 1 and 10; it can run at audio rates
Voltage control of the final attenuation: this voltage divided by 10V multiplies the Level knob, and the product is clamped between 0 and 1

outputs.text: The transformed signal after drive, clipping and level

menu: Oversample filter quality — 10th order by default, with 8th order and a cheaper 6th order; 10th and 8th cut at 80% of Nyquist and 6th at 50%
